finding: SC-002's pass bar is stated at three incompatible strengths across the line, and the weakest one is what 081d wires into DoD-9 and T017. The recorded verification ladder treats the fixture-level checker run as a REDUCED measurement and names the real bar: SC-002_why_reduced_insufficient reads 'a checker invocation on a fixture is not the review site's four-segment run; the R4R leg requires the review command itself', and SC-002_unblock reads 'run `/speckit.review` on `review-implemented-clean`'. T004 instead re-takes exactly that checker invocation (the one extracted from templates/commands/review.md:90, which is `--spec-dir <spec-dir> --json`), on the same fixture, and DoD-9 / T017 / tasks.md:247 declare that run sufficient for `pass`. The proposed measurement was already taken and closed by 081c's T004 leg (i) (tasks-081c.md:120, row marked [X]), so 081d's T004 adds no new evidence while flipping the verdict from `partial` to `pass`. This is the reduced-measurement-dressed-as-full class the feature exists to remove, applied to one of its own two `final` criteria.
evidence: I ran the checker read-only: `closure-acceptance-check.py --spec-dir tests/fixtures/acceptance-hardening/review-implemented-clean --json` -> verdict accept, claimed_status Implemented, final_path {pass 1, total 1}, all four completion_conditions true. That is the arc 081c already recorded as insufficient (verification.md:33 SC-002_why_reduced_insufficient, :35 SC-002_unblock). T004 (tasks.md:117) calls the same invocation 'SC-002's `Implemented -> Ready for Review` measurement at the review site'. No artifact reconciles the two.
recommendation: Decide the bar once, in one place. Either (a) run the real `/speckit.review` command over `review-implemented-clean` and record command / exit code / evidence path, which is what verification.md's ladder and SC-002_unblock already require; or (b) amend SC-002_why_reduced_insufficient to say the extracted fixture-level invocation IS the review site's judgement and justify why the four-segment run is not required for the R4R leg. Do not let T017 read `pass` off a measurement the ladder still calls insufficient.

finding: CHK030 confirmed by measurement, and stronger than reported. A 'mechanically derived domain-literal set' cannot distinguish an owner literal from an unrelated closed set's same-shaped literal, so 'zero unexempted hits' is false on any real tree. The measured hit set depends on which literals you decide to derive — which is itself proof that the derivation is not mechanical. With a deliberately narrow set (in-scope|signed-contract|user-waived|user-waiver|not-required|not-applicable|falsified|resolve-in-scope|this-slice|unverified) I get 11 files under templates/+shared/, of which at least four are unrelated vocabularies: sdd-routing-definitions.md:78 `not-required` is the traceability binary `required`/`not-required`; review-template.md:81/103/129 and templates/commands/review.md:110/117/131/151 `not-applicable` is the code-review segment-verdict four-value domain (pass | blocked | not-applicable | not-evaluated); expression-gates.md:85 `not-applicable` is the site-layer verdict; derivation-definitions.md:189 `in-scope` is ordinary English. With a broader set the count rises to 29 files.
evidence: grep -rlE '<narrow set>' templates/ shared/ -> 11 files: shared/constants/clarify-taxonomy.md, shared/definitions/derivation-definitions.md, shared/definitions/sdd-routing-definitions.md, shared/workflow/acceptance-hardening.md (owner), shared/workflow/expression-gates.md, shared/workflow/self-improvement-workflow.md, templates/commands/improve.md, templates/commands/review.md, templates/feature-details-template.md, templates/review-template.md, templates/verification-log-template.md. Broad set -> 29 files. The checklist's own reading (8 files / 7 non-owner) is a third count from a third set, which is the finding.
recommendation: The guard cannot be 'literal set == exemption list'. It must assert per-(literal, file) pairs, and the derivation must exclude literals that another closed set already owns. That exclusion is a decision the owner has to record — otherwise the guard's per-literal allow-list becomes a second definition point and violates FR-022 / AS-13, the very rule it guards. Cheapest decidable form: derive only literals that appear in the owner's OWN tables (not in Shared Strings' generic prose), and require a hit to be preceded by a documented ownership marker. If that is not attainable, narrow SC-009 ④ to what is attainable (limb (d) plus the projection narrowing) and say the zero-hit claim was withdrawn.

finding: CHK011 confirmed and sharpened. C-02 states `--spec-dir <dir>` is REQUIRED; tasks.md:257 discloses that in audit mode the root is `--repo` and `--spec-dir` is 'not required', and assigns the adjudication to a docstring that does not exist yet. GATE-6 (tasks.md:49) then invokes the audit in the single-feature CLI shape, `--spec-dir <spec-dir> --audit-existing`, which is the opposite of :257. Measured today: the mode check at :1296 fires BEFORE the `--spec-dir` requirement at :344, so `--audit-existing` with no `--spec-dir` exits 2 with the mode message, not the spec-dir message — i.e. `--spec-dir` is already unenforced in audit mode, silently. A future docstring cannot amend a MUST-level contract clause, and the row that will implement the mode is therefore free to pick either reading.
evidence: `closure-acceptance-check.py --audit-existing` -> exit 2 with 'input error: --audit-existing is not implemented in this slice ... (plan.md § Slice Boundary)'. With `--spec-dir tests/fixtures/acceptance-hardening/positive --audit-existing` -> exit 2 with the same message. Both prove the ordering and that the spec-dir requirement is not reached in audit mode. Contract text: C-02 (:13) 'MUST accept `--spec-dir <dir>` (required)'.
recommendation: Amend the contract at clause level in the same slice: C-02 becomes 'required except in `--audit-existing` mode, where the root is `--repo` (defaulting to the repository root) and `--spec-dir` MUST be rejected rather than ignored', or the reverse. Then change GATE-6 to the audit-mode invocation so the gate exercises the surface T013 builds. Whatever is decided, it belongs in C-02, not in T013's docstring, and the ordering must be explicit so a passing `--spec-dir` is not silently accepted by an audit run.

finding: CHK019 confirmed. 'Record `integration-record --result failed --reason closure-blocked`' and 'mark the line `blocked`' have mutually exclusive preconditions: integration-record requires state == completed (:1682), while A6 item 5 / SV-15 require integration-record to be structurally unreachable from `blocked`. Therefore exactly one order works — record first, then transition — and that order exists only as narrative sentence order in T008. T005, the single carrier for A6, asserts only unreachability 'from blocked'; it has no leg pinning the record-then-transition sequence, and GW-03 does not state it either. An implementer who marks first gets a red from T005 with no product text having required otherwise.
evidence: line-registry.py:1682 `require(entry.get('state') == 'completed', 'integration-record requires state=completed')`. _record_failed (:70-71) delegates to that action via the engine. integrate-lines.py:101-107 calls _record_failed(reg, line_id, 'quality-gate') and only then returns, with no state change. Recording a failed result sets `integration_result` and leaves `state` at `completed` (verified in the action body), so `update --state blocked` must follow.
recommendation: State the order as a constraint in T008 ('the `integration-record --result failed` call MUST execute while the line is still `completed`; the transition to `blocked` MUST follow it, because the record action refuses a blocked line'), and add one T005 leg that asserts the sequence end-to-end (record then update, final state `blocked`, `integration_result.result == failed`).

finding: CHK013 confirmed. C-03 defines claim resolution as a three-level order with the spec-local layer first (the spec dir's own `feature-detail.md`, then its `feature-registry.md`, then `.specify/memory/features.md` by key). Audit mode inverts the direction: it starts from registry rows and enumerates features, so the claim comes from the row being iterated. C-03 has no audit branch. If T011 ships the shape F-08 describes — a registry AND `.specify/specs/<key>/` subtrees — both paths are readable and nothing says which wins; the 15 existing cases only exercise the spec-local layer, so the corpus cannot answer it either.

recommendation: Add the audit branch to C-03 explicitly: 'in `--audit-existing` mode the claim is read from the registry row under audit; the spec-local layer is NOT consulted, so that the audit reports the registry's claim rather than a fixture-local override'. That sentence also decides F-08's ambiguity in favour of the registry being authoritative.

finding: CHK014 confirmed with one refinement. T011 makes the zero-write assertion out of two halves: a recursive hash over a `tmp_path` COPY of the fixture, and `git status --porcelain` over the repository. Because the audited tree is the copy, the repository query cannot observe writes to the audited tree — it is sensitive only to a checker that writes somewhere inside the repository checkout (and `--porcelain` excludes ignored paths, so a `.specify/.tmp/` or `__pycache__` write is invisible). So C-11's named verification is being applied to a different tree than the one under test, and the half that can actually break is the hash.
evidence: tasks.md:138 quoted; C-11 (contract:28) 'verified by `git status --porcelain` being unchanged across the run'; I confirmed `git status --porcelain` is clean on this tree before and after running the checker twice, which is the constant the half would report.
recommendation: Make the two halves observe the same subject: audit the in-repo fixture in place (which needs F-08's option (b) so the fixture is a valid audit root), keep the `tmp_path` copy hash as the breakable half, or state in C-11 that the named verification is unreachable for this case and that the hash replaces it. DoD-3's 'a run over the repository leaves `git status --porcelain` byte-identical' should then name which run.

finding: CHK022 confirmed. The same code point must now produce two different failure reasons and nothing says how they divide. Today integrate_line records `reason='quality-gate'` for any non-zero gate (:104) and that is the only gate-failure path. T008/GW-03 require `reason='closure-blocked'` when the closure judgement blocks, while also keeping `--gate-cmd` overridable — so an overridden gate's failure has no assigned reason. `closure-blocked` is also an unregistered literal: it appears nowhere outside the 081 spec, is in no `*_REASONS` constant (only `WAITING_REASONS` exists, :54), and `--reason` is free text, so nothing constrains its spelling. Finally SC-001 requires the driver site's named reason to be one of STR-008 / STR-009 / STR-014, which `closure-blocked` is not; no artifact says whether SC-001 reads the checker's output or the recorded integration reason at that site.
evidence: integrate-lines.py:101-107; `grep -rn 'closure-blocked' --include=*.py --include=*.md .` outside the 081 spec directory -> 0 hits; line-registry.py:54 `WAITING_REASONS = {'ownership-overlap','concurrency-cap'}`; requirements.md:203 (SC-001 closed set), :242-252 (Shared Strings, no `closure-blocked`).
recommendation: Decide three things in one place: (a) does `closure-blocked` replace `quality-gate` or is `quality-gate` retained for overridden gates — say which; (b) register `closure-blocked` as an owned literal (the declaring spec's § Shared Strings, or a `REASONS` constant beside `WAITING_REASONS`) so a test can pin its spelling; (c) state which field SC-001 reads at the driver site, so its 3/3 reading is not satisfiable by the checker's output while the recorded reason is something else.

finding: CHK026 confirmed. Five artifacts require the judgement to run 'at the feature line's closure and not per slice merge', but the merge unit in this engine IS the line: `integrate_line()` takes a line entry and `main` iterates lines (`--all`), so there is no per-slice merge event to gate. There is no branch to take wrongly and no behaviour that can go red. T007's own wording concedes this — 'the judgement runs at the feature line's closure, so **the doc surface says so** and the script does not gate every slice merge' — which turns the assertion into a documentation check, contradicting GW-08's 'every new gate MUST have a deterministic verdict produced by a program'.
evidence: tasks.md:119 (the sentence quoted), :35 (DoD-5), :124; plan.md:310; integrate-lines.py:211 `results.append(integrate_line(...))` inside a per-line loop.
recommendation: Either declare the obligation doc-only in GW-03 and DoD-5 (and stop asserting it in T007), or replace it with something a program can judge: e.g. assert that the gate's spec-dir input is derived from the line entry (F-06) and not from any argument supplied at integration-enqueue time, plus a leg that `--all` invokes the gate exactly once per line.

finding: CHK027 confirmed. GATE-5 fuses two different executions into one check: 'the gate command `integrate-lines.py` builds, run against `tests/fixtures/acceptance-hardening/negative`, exits non-zero with `closure-blocked` recorded and the line left `blocked`'. The first half (build the checker invocation and run it on a fixture) is executable and produces the non-zero exit; the second half (`closure-blocked` recorded, line `blocked`) only happens inside `integrate_line()`, which needs a registered line with `worktree_path`, a `rebase trunk`, and a gate run with `cwd=wt`. A fixture path alone cannot produce those readings, and the row does not say which invocation yields which assertion.
evidence: tasks.md:48; tasks.md:119 (same fusion in T007); integrate-lines.py:79-119 (worktree existence, rebase, then `run(['bash','-c',gate_cmd], cwd=wt)`).
recommendation: Split GATE-5 into GATE-5a (the extracted checker command over `negative` and `positive`; exit 1 with a closed-set reason / exit 0) and GATE-5b (a `tmp_path` registry + worktree drive of `integrate_line()` asserting `integration_result.result == failed`, `reason == closure-blocked`, and the resulting state `blocked`, with no `merged` record). Then T007 cites 5a and T008 cites 5b.

finding: CHK033 confirmed with a correction to its premise. FR-019 asks for a per-occurrence classification into 'new vocabulary use' or 'an unrelated pre-existing closed set', and treats 'exists but is classified' as a legal terminal state. SC-009 ④ asks for the same class of literals to have zero non-owner occurrences across templates/ and shared/, with a closed exemption list. The verdicts differ: FR-019 admits classified existence, SC-009 ④ admits only absence-or-exemption. The two literal sets are not identical (FR-019 is about `blocked` / `not-required`; SC-009 ④ derives the owner's whole column-name and value-domain set), so this is a partially overlapping pair — but no artifact says whether FR-019's classification ledger IS the guard's allowed list or a separate book. evidence: requirements.md:162 vs :211; tasks.md:100 (T002) and :141 (T014). Measured occurrence set for `blocked` under templates/+shared/ = 11 files, wider than either list.
recommendation: Make one of them authoritative: either the guard's allowed-surface list is generated from FR-019's classification (one artefact, one owner, Principle XIV satisfied), or FR-019's classification is declared a text obligation with no program reader. The second is cheaper and honest; say so in FR-019 and stop T002's output from being mistaken for the guard's input.

finding: CHK040 confirmed as an unclosed recurrence of 081c's CHK039. `resolved` is one of the three closed `Disposition` values, while T012 and § No Deferred Slice use it for a different reading — 'the row's carrier resolves against this tasks.md' — and write '3 of 3 resolved' beside three rows whose `Disposition` cells still read `inherited` (plan.md:236-238).
